newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African vigilantes divert police from criminals.
newsitem.headline: S.African vigilantes divert police from criminals.

text.p: Police minister Sydney Mufamadi criticised South Africa's Moslem-based vigilante movement on Wednesday, saying it was diverting police from acting against criminals.

He said in a statement that People Against Gangsterism and Drugs (PAGAD) had staged 50 marches to the homes of alleged drug dealers in the Cape Town area in the last five months, all of which had to be escorted by police at great cost in time and money.

"This is all the more disconcerting if one considers that the personnel, money and vehicles could have been used to improve visible pro-active policing initiatives against drug, gang and (other) crime," Mufamadi said.
PAGAD spokesman Aslam Toefy told reporters on Wednesday the movement planned to conduct a "drug awareness" programme on Monday at Cape Town international airport.
He said police and the airport management had given permission for the event, which he said would not be a demonstration and would not disrupt tourism.
"We will not carry guns and we will not be masked," Toefy said. "The airport has everything to do with drugs. We need dogs and scanners there to monitor what is coming in."

President Nelson Mandela told a news conference on Sunday that PAGAD had overstepped the mark in its anti-crime campaign and ruled out demonstrations at airports or other places where tourists gather.
Mufamadi said PAGAD's activities were themselves often illegal and included murder, attempted murder, assault and intimidation.
"I know of no other community-based anti-crime organisation in the country... against whose members or supporters such a wide range of serious criminal charges are being investigated," he said.
"We have reached the stage where it can be said without any doubt that PAGAD activities have undermined the ability of the police to fight drug- and gang-related crime," Mufamadi said.
